minutes.headline: Commission heard that the bylaw's only real enforcement against demolition by neglect is court, and chose to explore a lighter fine option with Town Counsel.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met with a zoning/building official on Zoom to discuss how to enforce the bylaw against demolition by neglect. The official said the bylaw has no property maintenance code or nuisance bylaw behind it, so enforcement means a cease and desist letter and then court. The commission also approved prior minutes, discussed the Town Hall chimney bid, the master plan steering committee, a district brochure, and signage and walking tour ideas.

budget_items.topic: Freedoms Way National Heritage Area matching grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair described a reimbursable matching grant, rolling applications, that might help a private owner of a historic property. He will email thoughts and ask the executive director about the schedule.
The single bid for the project came in far above the amount appropriated at town meeting. This raises concern about the Ritter building project budget.

budget_items.topic: Fines under a nuisance or 21D non-criminal bylaw
budget_items.what_was_said: Brian said a zoning-style or 21D enforcement route allows daily fines that can be waived if work proceeds. The APD bylaw lacks that language now.
Lunenburg did not adopt CPA, so those funds are unavailable to help owners; members suggested grants or CPA later as a source of repair help.

decisions.decision: Commission will pursue a conversation with Town Counsel, with Brian willing to attend, about adding a 21D-style fine option to the bylaw.
The chair will find the Town Counsel meeting schedule and notify members.
With members' concurrence, the chair will ask the facilities manager to report on the chimney phase tied to the Town Hall conditional approval.
The chair will email the draft brochure outline for members to edit, aiming to mail it within the district before the end of the calendar year.
January meeting to be devoted to reviewing the National Register nomination to identify resources for communication, markers and signs.
Next meeting set for the 14th of November, with one member noting a conflict.

what_happened.line: The Commission was told the bylaw has no property maintenance code or nuisance bylaw behind it, so enforcing against demolition by neglect means a cease and desist letter, then court.
The Commission agreed to pursue a conversation with Town Counsel about adding a fine option, modelled on the non-criminal 21D approach, to the bylaw.
The single bid for the Town Hall chimney work came in far above the amount appropriated, and the chair will ask the facilities manager to report on the chimney phase.
Lunenburg has not adopted the Community Preservation Act, so those funds are unavailable to help owners with repairs.
The chair will email a draft district brochure outline for edits, and the January meeting will review the National Register nomination for signs and markers.

why_it_matters: Historic buildings in the district have little protection from neglect short of a court case, and a fine option would need a bylaw change that voters at Town Meeting would be asked to approve.
A chimney bid well above the appropriation for Town Hall could mean a request for more money at a future Town Meeting.

The facilities manager's report on the Town Hall chimney phase.
